claims: Artemis II will launch from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
Artemis II will execute a 10-day "figure-8" free-return trajectory around the Moon.
The Orion spacecraft will orbit Earth twice—the second being a wider, high-altitude loop.
The Orion spacecraft will use a Translunar Injection burn to slingshot toward the Moon.
The Orion spacecraft will splash down in the Pacific Ocean.
Orion launches on the SLS rocket.
Orion enters a high-elliptical Earth orbit with perigee 563 km and apogee 70,000 km.
Orion performs system checkouts and maneuvers near the upper stage.
Translunar Injection (TLI) is a burn at perigee.
Translunar Injection boosts the spacecraft out of Earth orbit towards the Moon.
The craft loops around the far side of the Moon roughly 5,000 miles (8,000 km) above the surface.
The craft does not enter lunar orbit.
Gravity will return the craft to Earth.
The spacecraft utilizes a "skip-entry" technique to manage speeds of 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
Artemis II is set to fly further from Earth than any previous human mission.
Artemis II surpasses the 252,799-mile record from Earth.
The surpassing potentially occurs during its lunar flyby.
The total mission lasts approximately 10 days.
